title: Plane: Ancient Planes You Can Visit
meta_description: Three planes with the species left open: a Hague tree above a Roman port town, a Hoorn tree with a bare 1871 planting date, and a Bratislava forest giant.
intro: Three planes on this map carry only their genus, Platanus, because whichever register or record named them stopped at that. The Hague's Plane of Park Hoekenburg grows over Forum Hadriani, a Roman port town whose excavation once turned up an oak post felled in the year 212, read straight off its rings. Hoorn's Plane of Number 37 has the opposite problem: an exact planting date, 1871, at the waterside of the Oosterpoortsgracht, but no species beyond plane. Bratislava's Plane of Kysucká Street stands where nobody planted it for show, on the road up to Zelezna studnicka, protected tree number 231, measured at 6.11 metres round in 2012. Planes hybridise readily and the parents can be hard to call from bark and leaf alone, which is likely why all three were left at genus. If you can tell an Oriental plane from a London plane on sight, tell us.
